name: Hollow terracotta block
summary: A building block of clay that has webs inside. A maker presses it in a mould, so that it dries and fires without a crack and weighs little.
how: Press the clay in a plaster mould to the shape and the relief of the block.
Leave the back open and add webs inside, with a wall of 25 to 50 mm.
Dry the block slowly, then fire it hard at about 1100 °C.
Bed the block in mortar and tie it to the backing wall or the steel frame.

origin.note: English makers in Lambeth and Staffordshire start to sell pressed terracotta blocks for buildings.

adoptions.via: Makers in London and Leeds press hollow terracotta blocks for museums, schools and town halls.
Chicago works make thin, hollow terracotta tile that hangs on the steel frame of a tall building.
